questions.prompt: You want scheduled maintenance to suppress notifications for one VM while preserving fired-alert records. Which approach fits?

options.text: A scheduled alert processing rule suppressing its action groups.
options.explanation: This processes fired alerts without disabling condition evaluation.

options.text: Disable every alert rule in the subscription.
options.explanation: That stops evaluation broadly and loses intended alert firing.

options.text: Delete the collected metrics during maintenance.
options.explanation: Suppression does not require data deletion.
That changes collection rather than a scheduled response policy.

questions.prompt: Can one alert processing rule directly scope resources from a different subscription than its own?

options.text: Yes, any subscription in the tenant.
options.explanation: The documented scope stays within its subscription.

options.text: No; its scoped resources must be in the same subscription.
options.explanation: Create suitable processing rules in the relevant subscriptions.

options.text: Yes, if they have identical resource-group names.
options.explanation: Matching names do not override subscription scope.

options.text: Yes, if the action group uses email.
options.explanation: Response type does not change processing-rule scope.

questions.prompt: Will an Azure Monitor alert processing rule suppress Azure Service Health alerts?

options.text: Yes, all alert sources are affected without exception.
options.explanation: Service Health is a documented exception.

options.text: Yes, if the schedule is recurring.
options.explanation: Schedule type does not remove that exception.

options.text: No; processing rules do not affect Service Health alerts.
options.explanation: Plan Service Health notification behavior separately.

options.text: Yes, if its scope is the whole subscription.
options.explanation: Broad scope does not override the exclusion.
